verified_uncited_book_records.text: The entry calls 上 an indicative graph. Its oracle-bone forms place a short horizontal mark above a longer reference line; the bronze form continues this pattern. Spring-and-Autumn forms add a vertical stroke, which the entry identifies as the basis of the clerical form. Warring States forms vary: some add decorative strokes or omit the upper short mark, while others add 是 or 止 as meaning determinatives, yielding forms analyzed as 从是或止、上声. The entry gives the original meaning as spatial, opposite 下, and reports extensions to high places, heaven, and ruler. Checked the 上 headword, numbered glyph sequence and labels, prose through the end of the entry, and the transition to 帝 against the attached original-resolution scan. PDF page 15 begins 帝, not a continuation of 上. The diagrams cite 《甲文编》 p.3, 《金文编》 p.5, 《类编》 p.2, 《楚系简帛》 p.17, 《古文典》 p.656, 《汉语字形表》 p.3, 《说文》 p.7, and 《篆隶表》 p.3; those cited pages were not separately inspected.
